Kimi-Linear hybrid decode — official speedup 0.8334× (LOW)
Memory summary

The reconstructed final solution implements a Triton W4A16 dequant-GEMV and a reference-compatible Kimi-Linear block with three KDA layers, one MLA layer, and MoE routing. The recorded correctness check passed, but the benchmark result was 0.8334× speedup—slower than baseline at all three contexts, graded LOW. The GPU reported during the run was an H100, not the specified RTX PRO 6000, and the benchmark was contended.

Relevant prior context

The solution uses one Triton GEMV kernel per projection: it unpacks low and high int4 nibbles, applies the group scale and zero point, and accumulates output tiles without materializing bf16 weights. The accompanying QuantLinear, QuantExperts, KDA, MLA, MoE, block, and model classes preserve reference-style buffers and interfaces.

The standalone GEMV check reported ALL OK and cosine similarity 0.999997. The full check.py run reported PASS for seeds 0, 1, and 2 at contexts 2048 and 8192; output cosine was at least 0.9998 and state similarities were 1.0000.

The run investigated an MLA absorb formulation and reducing launch overhead, but the reconstructed final code still materializes the full MLA cache projection with st["c_kv"] @ self.kv_b.weight_bf(). Its MoE loops over the eight routed experts and shared expert, issuing separate GEMVs for gate, up, and down projections. Thus the implementation does not achieve a single fused GPU kernel for the whole timed step.

NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, 9.0

The benchmark target was RTX PRO 6000 (SM120 Blackwell). A concurrent benchmark was also using the GPU. The run attributed its roughly 10 ms/token timings to contention; the recorded speedup ratio was still below 1×, though contention makes the measurements noisy.

No separate final solution file, official result file, or audit file was published. Recording summary

The reconstructed solution’s main kernel is _w4_gemv_kernel: for each output tile and 128-element input group, it loads packed weights and bf16 scale/zero values, accumulates low- and high-nibble products, subtracts the zero-point correction, and stores bf16 output. Batch-1 quantized linears use this kernel; non-vector inputs materialize dequantized weights. KDA updates its recurrent and short-convolution state. MLA appends to its cache and attends over materialized kv_b projections. MoE computes top-8 routing plus the shared expert through Python loops and individual GEMV calls.
